summary: Brad Warner is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Wadsworth High School and Kent State University, he studied under Tim McCarthy, Gyomay Kubose, and Gudō Wafu Nishijima. He led Dogen Sangha International (2007) and founded Dogen Sangha Los Angeles (2012).

Bradford Lyman Phillips specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Naropa University, Harvard University (M.T.S., 1993), and the University of Virginia (B.A., 1989; Ph.D., 2004) under Michael Aris, Jeffrey Hopkins, Cecil Y. Lang, and David F. Germano.

Bradley L. Herling is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. His academic appointments include Assistant Director at Boston University and a post at Marymount Manhattan College, attested in 2008.

Braj Basi Lal was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad and trained under Mortimer Wheeler (1943). He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of IIAS (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and his habilitation at the University of Munich. He held posts at SOAS (~2005–2010) and Munich (~2010–2017).
Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015), where he studied under advisor Patrick Arthur Pranke.

Bratindra Nath Mukherjee (1932–2013) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at the University of Calcutta, Cambridge, and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and others, he served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at Calcutta (1975–1998).

Brendan S. Gillon is an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Around 1992, he served as an associate professor in the Department of Linguistics at McGill University.

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Vanderbilt and Kyoto University, held research posts at Otani and Kyoto, and taught at Shiga, Kwansei Gakuin, and Loyola University Maryland (attested 2007, 2018).
Brian Bocking is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds, where he studied under Michael Pye.
Brian Cutillo (1945–2006) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1963–1967) and under Ngawang Wangyal.

Brian D. Ruppert works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Mentored by Willis Stoesz, he held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2019) and Bates College (~2019) as Kazushige Hirasawa Professor and Asian Studies Program Chair.

Brian Daizen Victoria is a Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history scholar. Educated at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, Eihei-ji, and Temple, he held posts at Auckland, Antioch (2005–2013), Adelaide, and as an Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies Fellow (2013).
Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. He earned his PhD in 2005 at Indiana University, where he studied under his doctoral supervisor, György Kara.

Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was an Indologist and Tibetologist educated at The King's School, Haileybury/East India Company College, and Fort William College. He served as Assistant Resident (1820) and British Resident in Nepal (1821; 1833–1843).

Brian J. Nichols specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and earned his PhD at Rice University (attested 2011) under doctoral supervisor Anne Carolyn Klein.

Bridget Allchin was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Cape Town and UCL (PhD 1950) under Frederick Zeuner. She was a fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge (~1969–2017) and held leadership roles at the Ancient India & Iran Trust.
Brigitte Marschall completed her doctoral promotion at the University of Vienna and later served there as a professor (attested 2010).
Brigitte Steinmann is a Tibetologist who studied under Alexander W. Macdonald and traditional teacher Bahadur Singh. She held an academic post at the University of Montpellier, attested in 2004.

Bronwyn Finnigan specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Auckland, Melbourne, and Sydney under John Bishop and Rosalind Hursthouse, she held posts at Auckland, Marquette University (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (2014).
